scope: Small hand-audited original-paraphrase seed corpus for routing and QA; intentionally non-exhaustive.

units.principle: Mild, recoverable stress can activate adaptive maintenance and defense responses, while more intense or persistent stress is not assumed to be beneficial.
risks: Do not infer that more fasting, heat, cold, exercise, pain, or deprivation produces more benefit.
limitations: Review-level synthesis; intervention effects remain stressor-, dose-, population-, and outcome-specific.

locator.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain

units.principle: Short-term stress responses can support adaptation, but repeated or poorly recovered activation can accumulate as allostatic load and increase physiological wear.
risks: Chronic distress, sleep loss, illness, injury, trauma, or severe mental-health symptoms must not be reframed as useful hormesis.
limitations: Allostatic mechanisms are multi-system and individual; a single consumer metric cannot establish clinical allostatic load.

units.principle: Emotion and bodily state interact bidirectionally; interoceptive signals can influence feelings while brain appraisal and regulation can also shape physiological responses.
risks: Do not reduce distress to mindset alone or imply that emotional regulation can replace indicated clinical care.
limitations: Mechanisms do not imply that every subjective feeling maps uniquely to a measurable physiological state.
